title: Weak dimension at most one and valuation local rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. The following are equivalent: (i) for every $R$-module $M$ there are flat $R$-modules $F_0,F_1$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $R$-linear maps $F_1\xrightarrow{a}F_0\xrightarrow{b}M$ with $a$ injective, $b$ surjective, and $\operatorname{im}(a)=\ker(b)$ (a flat resolution of length at most one); (ii) for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a valuation domain [def-trf-valuation-ring]. In particular, for a nonzero local commutative ring $R$ (one with a unique maximal ideal), condition (i) is equivalent to $R$ itself being a valuation domain. No Noetherian or dimension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, equivalence (1) and (5); Tag 092D, definition-weak-dimension, and the proof (4) implies (1) giving a length-one flat resolution.

proof.text: Assume (i) and fix an ideal $I\subseteq R$. Apply (i) to $R/I$, writing $0\to F_1\xrightarrow{a}F_0\xrightarrow{b}R/I\to0$. Choose $x\in F_0$ with $b(x)=1+I$ and put $E=\{(u,r)\in F_0\oplus R:b(u)=r+I\}$. The map $F_1\oplus R\to E$, $(v,r)\mapsto(a(v)+rx,r)$, is an isomorphism: given $(u,r)$, exactness gives a unique $v$ with $a(v)=u-rx$. Thus $E$ is flat. Indeed, tensoring any injection with $F_1\oplus R$ is the direct sum of its tensor with $F_1$ and itself, under $n\otimes(v,r)\mapsto(n\otimes v,rn)$; the inverse is the sum of the two component inclusions, so this map is injective by the flatness definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (1) implies (2); elementary pullback comparison of the supplied length-one resolution with $R	o R/I$.

proof.text: Projection $E\to F_0$ is surjective: lift $b(u)\in R/I$ to $r\in R$. Its kernel consists exactly of $(0,r)$ with $r\in I$. Therefore $0\to I\to E\to F_0\to0$ is short exact. Both $E$ (step 1) and $F_0$ are flat, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ses-kernel-flat] makes $I$ flat. This proves that (i) implies flatness of every ideal, with no finite-generation assumption on $I$.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (1) implies (2); Tag 00HM, algebra-lemma-flat-ses, second assertion.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ and write $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$. For any ideal $J\subseteq A$, let $I=\{r\in R:r/1\in J\}$. By [lem-trf-module-submodule-localization], $J=I_{\mathfrak p}$ inside $A$; step 2 makes $I$ flat over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], $A\otimes_R I$ is flat over $A$. Its identification with $I_{\mathfrak p}$ sends $(r/s)\otimes i$ to $ri/s$, with inverse $i/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes i$; the fraction relations and balancing relation give mutual inverses. Hence every ideal of $A$ is flat. The ring $A$ is nonzero and local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA$, by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; nonzeroness also follows directly since $1/1=0$ would force $0\notin\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (1) implies (5); localization of ideals, Tags 00CU and 00HI.

proof.text: Continue with $A$ from step 3. Every finitely generated ideal is free by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free], applied using its flatness and the locality of $A$. A nonzero free ideal has exactly one basis element: an empty basis would give the zero ideal, while two distinct basis elements $u,v\in J\subseteq A$ satisfy $v\cdot u-u\cdot v=0$, contradicting independence (their coefficients force $u=v=0$). Thus every nonzero finitely generated ideal is principal with a generator $h$ for which $ch=0$ forces $c=0$. If $0\ne f\in A$, apply this to $(f)=(h)$ and write $f=ah$, $h=bf$. Then $(1-ba)h=0$, so $ba=1$ and $a$ is a unit. Therefore $f$ is a nonzerodivisor. Since $A\ne0$, it is a domain. The zero ideal is principal too.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (1) implies (5), finite-flat-local and rank-one argument; Tag 00NZ.

proof.text: For nonzero $f,g\in A$, step 4 gives $(f,g)=(h)$ with $h\ne0$. Write $f=ah$, $g=bh$, $h=cf+dg$. Cancelling $h$ in the domain gives $ca+db=1$. At least one of $a,b$ is a unit: otherwise both belong to the unique maximal ideal of the local ring $A$, contradicting this equality. If $a$ is a unit then $g/f=b/a\in A$, and if $b$ is a unit then $f/g=a/b\in A$. Every nonzero element of $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ is such an $f/g$, so $A$ is a valuation domain by [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Since $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary, this proves (ii).

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (1) implies (5); explicit algebra of Tag 090Q, algebra-lemma-characterize-valuation-ring.

proof.text: Assume (ii) and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, which is prime, exactness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] applied to $0\to I\to R$ embeds $I_{\mathfrak m}$ into the domain $A=R_{\mathfrak m}$. Hence $I_{\mathfrak m}$ is torsion-free over $A$: if $0\ne a\in A$ kills $z$, its image in $A$ satisfies $az=0$, so $z=0$. By (ii), $A$ is a valuation domain; [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] makes $I_{\mathfrak m}$ flat over $A$. The localization scalar comparison [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] makes it flat over $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-base-flatness-maximal-localizations] with $C=R$ and $N=I$ to conclude that $I$ is flat over $R$. This also handles the zero ring: the local hypotheses are vacuous and that cited statement explicitly allows zero rings.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (5) implies (3), with the stronger torsion-free flatness input Tag 0539; Tag 00HT, algebra-lemma-flat-localization, parts (2),(4).

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq P$ with $P$ flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion], to prove $N$ flat it suffices, for every finitely generated ideal $J$, to prove that $\mu_N:J\otimes_R N\to N$ is injective. Step 6 says that $J$ is flat. Thus the map $J\otimes_R N\to J\otimes_R P$ induced by $N\hookrightarrow P$ is injective by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], using tensor symmetry $j\otimes n\leftrightarrow n\otimes j$. The map $\mu_P:J\otimes_R P\to P$ is injective by the same flat-ideal criterion, since $P$ is flat. Their composite equals $J\otimes_R N\xrightarrow{\mu_N}N\hookrightarrow P$: both send $j\otimes n$ to $jn$. An injective composite has an injective first factor, so $\mu_N$ is injective, proving $N$ flat.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (2) implies (4); direct tensor-square proof of this implication as in Ring.WeakDimensionLEOne.flat_submodule.

proof.text: For any $R$-module $M$, take the free module $F=\bigoplus_{m\in M}R$ of finitely supported families and the surjection $q:F\to M$, $(r_m)\mapsto\sum_m r_m m$ (the vector supported at $m$ with coefficient $1$ maps to $m$). By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], $F$ is flat. Step 7 makes $K=\ker(q)\subseteq F$ flat. Then the inclusion and $q$ give $0\to K\to F\to M\to0$, with exactly the injectivity, surjectivity and image-kernel equality required in (i). No finite generation of $M$ or $F$ is used.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, (4) implies (1), construction of a free surjection and its flat kernel.

proof.text: For the local assertion, suppose first that the nonzero local ring $R$ satisfies (i). Steps 1--2 make its ideals flat; the arguments of steps 4--5 apply directly with $A=R$ and prove it a valuation domain. Conversely, let $R$ itself be a valuation domain. Every ideal $J\subseteq R$ is torsion-free by cancellation in $R$, hence flat by [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat]. The tensor-square argument of step 7 now applies using this ideal flatness, and the construction of step 8 gives (i). This proves the local assertion without assuming that $R$ is Noetherian or has finite Krull dimension.

source.place: Tag 092S, lemma-weak-dimension-at-most-1, local case of (3) implies (5), and (5) implies (3); Tag 0539.

lean.statement: theorem flat_resolution_length_one_iff_prime_localizations_valuation (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, ∃ F₀ F₁ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.Flat R F₀ ∧ Module.Flat R F₁ ∧ ∃ (a : F₁ →ₗ[R] F₀) (b : F₀ →ₗ[R] M), Function.Injective a ∧ Function.Surjective b ∧ LinearMap.range a = LinearMap.ker b) ↔ ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], ∃ h : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p), @ValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime p) _ h
lean.note: The second declaration states the final nonzero local-ring clause.
